key_insight: This paper gives the first complete fixed-domain asymptotic theory for joint maximum likelihood estimation of RBF-kernel Gaussian process variance, lengthscale, and nugget parameters, proving consistency, rates, and asymptotic normality.
engineering_relevance: It provides the theoretical basis for trusting and tuning GP hyperparameter estimates in scientific computing, optimization, and spatial/time-series modeling when data are densely sampled in a bounded domain.
method: Analyze the joint MLE of GP spatial variance, lengthscale, and nugget under fixed-domain asymptotics.
Prove consistency, derive parameter-specific convergence rates, and establish joint asymptotic normality.
Show the obtained rates are minimax optimal.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a complete asymptotic characterization of the MLEs, including consistency, convergence rates, and joint asymptotic normality, but does not mention empirical experiments.
watch_item: The results are asymptotic and fixed-domain-specific, so practical performance may differ for finite samples or increasing-domain settings.
paper_title: Sharp Asymptotic Theory of Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Gaussian Processes with an RBF Kernel
